kmp/errorCodes.means: the arguments cannot produce a call; fix them — retrying unchanged cannot work
the memory asked for is not in this store

the operation conflicted with current state; follow the message — a retryable write conflict is safely replayed with the same idempotency key, while a key already accepted with different content must not be reused
the kernel could not be reached; the same call may work later
no such tool on this surface
the kernel failed for a reason the arguments cannot fix

tools.description: Write memory with evidence. Use memories for one or more records with local ids, labels and justified links, validated as one packet before canonical ingest. Use relations to link memories that already exist: the kernel validates the stored endpoints and writes only the link and its evidence. Never resubmit a stored memory as a record just to connect it. Omit options.dry_run for normal writes. Rich links, including local links, return needs_review with brief stored context before commit. Review it and use the returned continuation; changed context refreshes the review. Independent observations and honest fallback links remain one call. Set it to true only for an explicitly requested preview or payload debugging. Reach for kmp_ingest only when producing the exact graph yourself. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic write.
tools.name: kmp_write_memory

accepted.description: True only when the canonical ingest was committed; false for a preview or pending context review.

evidence.description: Evidence nodes created by this write. Their ids are derived from the logical write identity and the triple, so an exact retry replays onto the same node and a later link to the same pair adds a new one instead of overwriting it.

relations.description: Links this relation-only write brought into existence: from, rel, to, class, confidence, the observation the link itself carries, and the evidence node created with it. Absent observed_at means the kernel stamped its ingestion instant, never an endpoint's clock.

unchanged_sources.description: The endpoint refs this relation-only write leaves untouched. Source text, evidence, coordinates, labels, metadata and ingestion history are not rewritten.

entries.description: Memories needing implicit observation, counted once across labels.

observed_at.description: ingested_at: omitted/null observation is resolved by the kernel. Previews describe a plan, never a committed timestamp.

provenance.description: Packet provenance also defaults to this write's ingestion time; search-summary updates preserve original fact clocks.

scope.description: submitted_packet: coverage of the declaration only.

source_coverage.description: not_assessed: KMP cannot detect facts omitted by the writer.

diagnostics.description: Planner diagnostics that qualify the write.

dry_run.description: Whether this response is a validated preview that wrote nothing.

expand_context.description: Native reads only for stored_abouts to expand omitted stored surroundings. Complete their relevant pages.

feedback.description: Validation signals. Codes and paths come from validation, not message parsing. A warning can accompany acceptance; never invent missing proof.

arguments.description: Complete arguments to execute that read.

tool.description: Supported reading move, not proof that the proposed relation holds.

allowed_values.description: Valid vocabulary when the refused field has one; choose using the source, never automatically substitute a kind.

expected_type.description: JSON type required by an INVALID_TYPE refusal, such as array or object.

field.description: Argument path, for example memories[1].evidence; empty denotes the request as a whole.

reason.description: What must be corrected using actual sources.

received_type.description: Actual JSON type at the refused field; a JSON-encoded string remains string and is never coerced.

severity.description: error for a refusal; warning for accepted relations whose prior context needs review.

generated_refs.description: Stable refs generated for entries whose ref the caller omitted. Their identity suffix is deterministic for an exact logical-write retry and distinct across different writes.

ingest_preview.description: Canonical kmp_ingest arguments. Present only on dry-run.

created.description: Of those, the labels the about did not hold before this write. Present only after a committed write; vocabulary grows here, so read it.

resembling.description: After a committed non-strict write: the labels written that resemble one the about already held, each with `key`, `value`, `existing_key`, `existing_value`, `kind` and `why`. Under strict such a write is refused instead, naming both labels, unless `options.labels_new` insists.

written.description: The labels this write carries, each `key` and `value`, in the order their coordinates were emitted.

local_refs.description: For a memories packet, local id to canonical memory ref. Preview refs are planned; accepted=true confirms persistence.

neighborhood.description: Bounded literal context: stored/proposed items, exact refs, clocks, reasons, omissions, token and complete stored_abouts ownership. Proximity does not prove a relation; expand partial stored context when needed.

next_actions.description: For needs_review, the bound write continuation. Review first; resuming rechecks context. No human approval per write is required.

next_suggested_reads.description: Optional preview reading suggestions. Accepted writes need no routine verification; receipt.action retrieves audit detail on demand.

proposed_relations.description: Committed memories on a store with write-relations.json: relations Jev reads as missing from them, as `review_token`, `items` ({`item_id`, `from`, `to`, `rel`, `confidence`, `to_excerpt`}) and `jev`. Nothing is written: declare the ones you confirm with kmp_curate apply, in your own why and evidence.

read_after_write_ready.description: Whether a read now observes the accepted write.

arguments.description: Complete arguments. object.text holds JSON with receipt.canonical_memory, receipt.writer diagnostics and command revision/hash. It is a historical snapshot, not current graph state.

tool.description: kmp_inspect; execute only when accepted detail is needed.

ref.description: Immutable accepted-command audit ref. Absent for previews and simulated backends.

relation_quality.description: Preview per-relation validation. After commit, recover it with receipt.action.

relation_quality_metrics.description: Preview counts and prior-context coverage; stored in the receipt after commit.

relations.description: Compiled source -> relation -> target triples, in canonical ingest order. @id resolves through local_refs; other endpoints remain canonical refs. Review direction and scope against the source: acceptance does not prove semantic fidelity.

from.description: Source memory, the containing record in the request.

memories.description: Memories this packet wrote at a ref the caller supplied, each with the evidence this write put on it and the observation it now carries. A supplied ref replaces whatever that entry held; use relations to add a link without replacing a source.

not_stored.description: Why no expansion could be judged or kept: nothing is stored unjudged.

refused.description: Each refused expansion as {ref, expansion, why}: the lint's fault or Jev's reading.

stored.description: Memory ref to the expansions kept, each read by Jev as belonging to it at the store's bar.

status.description: committed appended a command; replayed returned its earlier acceptance; validated is a preview; needs_review has applied nothing and returns context to review; rejected failed validation. unconfirmed cannot establish persistence: retain the logical key when resolving a transport failure.

summary.description: Counts and scope of the semantic write the planner prepared.

scope.description: current_store for a live embedded/gRPC preview; fixture for a simulated backend. A successful preview is not a reservation or a commit.

tell_the_user.description: One-time handoff text for the human; it is not another kernel instruction.

url.description: Loopback, read-only viewer URL carrying this session's capability.

warnings.description: Store notices qualifying this preview or accepted write; retain them.

tools.description: Return a compact Kernel Memory Protocol wake packet for continuing work. scope distinguishes selected proof from about context: time bounds apply to the selection, while summary, current_state, semantic next actions and labels can include other times. Requested dimensions apply to both. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic wake.
tools.name: kmp_wake

labels.description: The catalogue of the abouts this wake read: every label their entries stand in, as `about`, `key` (the dimension kind), `value` (the scope id), `entries` and `last_observed_at`. The current about first, then by use. Read it before naming a label on a new memory, so an existing one is reused instead of guessed. The most used labels are the first expansion the packet fills; the rest follow the causal spine, and `projection` reports what did not fit. Nothing of the core is shortened to make room for a label.

budget.description: The normative byte ceiling, bytes actually used, and retained token-planning hint.

contract.description: The projection contract version, e.g. kmp.recall.projection.v3.

core_reused.description: Present and true on a continuation that omits the stable core: it carries only new expansion items. Combine them with the first page's core and earlier pages; page.repeat_core=true returns the core again.

core_text_shortened.description: Whether stable core prose had to be shortened to fit max_bytes.

detail.description: compact | balanced | full — the detail tier that was served.

excluded_by_detail.description: Excluded by detail tier, not truncation; increase budget.detail to include them.

more_on_request.description: Present on an answered ask: proof past its cited core left unpaged; budget.detail=full pages it.

next_action.description: Execute this call unchanged. A continuation is {continuation}: a handle the server resolves to the complete call, cursor included. A restart when core_text_shortened is the complete call without page.cursor, recovering the full core. The proposed allowance is sufficient; keep the result partial if unavailable. Null when neither action remains.

arguments.description: Either {continuation} or the complete bound request; both preserve question, original wording, clock, interval and dimension filters.

has_more.description: More items remain; this page is incomplete.

minimum_progress_bytes.description: When stalled or core_text_shortened, a sufficient byte allowance for the unshortened core and expansion progress. The returned action adds 10000 bytes for useful expansion instead of negotiating only one item.

next_cursor.description: Opaque recall cursor (kmp2) for page.cursor, or null: it resumes after the item this page ended on. Keep bound arguments unchanged; only page.entries, budget.tokens and budget.max_bytes may vary. A kmp1 cursor is refused as outdated (READ_CURSOR_OUTDATED): restart.

offset.description: Number of eligible expansion items reconstructed by earlier pages.

total.description: Total eligible expansion items in the selection.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when the ask's ranking holds more than this reading carries (kmp2 lazy pages): total and sections.*.remaining are lower bounds and has_more is true.

sections.description: Per-section counts; a zero counter and a section with none are omitted. core and excluded_by_detail appear on the page that carries the core; returned_on_page and remaining on every page. remaining counts eligible expansion after this page, excluding the core and prior pages. eligible = core + all returned_on_page + last remaining; total = eligible + excluded_by_detail. Zero does not prove sufficient evidence; core_text_shortened, detail and selection caps still qualify coverage.

selection_omitted.description: Items excluded by budget.max_entries before paging.

abouts_empty_in_selection.description: Searched abouts with no entry in the selected interval or effective at the selected instant; empty for an unbounded read.

abouts_selected.description: Abouts read under dimensions.scope, current one first. Refs retain ownership; this list distinguishes searched from unsearched abouts.

as_of.description: Selected instant, including the time resolved from a ref cursor; null if unrequested.

axis.description: Selected occurred/observed/ingested/validity clock, or default precedence; null at the memory's own frontier.

confidence.description: Wake uses medium for a non-empty deterministic retrieval packet; this is not relation-writer certainty.

conflicts.description: Explicit contradictions whose entries are both still live; distinct from supersession.

evidence.description: Verbatim stored text; metadata.proof_role distinguishes claim from evidence. Retrieval metadata never changes that text. reached_by items are indirect proof, never answers or citations in because; reached_from, reached_via and reached_hops identify their route. On citations, bridged_terms names cross-language word pairs; restated_from and restated_via identify a writer-declared restatement; matched_via: summary and summary_terms identify words matched through the writer's English summary_en, not the canonical text.

expired.description: Entries past exclusive valid_until at the temporal cursor, recall as_of/interval end, or otherwise the memory's latest instant. Expiry needs no replacement.

frontier_size.description: Reachable items not returned; a signal to expand.

matched_relations.description: Typed relations contributing to ordering. Their prose may improve a match, never promote unrelated evidence into an answer.

missing.description: What was sought but not found: no retrieval or no evidence bearing on the question. Non-empty with UNKNOWN.

nearest_outside.description: On interval UNKNOWN, nearest match outside it: ref, time and axis. Distinguishes not then from not known; otherwise null.

superseded.description: Replaced entries with superseded_by and why. Historical state, distinct from contradiction; not current advice. An ask's core keeps those touching a cited memory; the rest page as section proof.superseded.

resume_cursor.description: Newest temporal coordinate covered by this packet; null when the packet carries no temporal anchor.

context.description: Response paths from the about context after dimensional filtering, before temporal selection. They can describe earlier or later memories; do not treat them as the selected historical state.

context_time.description: Context does not apply the requested as_of or interval.

anyOf.description: Applied dimensional selection with explicit mode and scope defaults. Both proof and about context use it. The catalogue retains those entries' labels; a predicate does not filter individual catalogue labels. Null means the backend supplied no selection metadata.

abouts.description: Non-empty selection for scope=abouts. Include the current about if wanted.

scope.description: Default current_about stays inside about. abouts reads the named list with separate ownership; selection neither merges abouts nor authorizes cross-about links. all_abouts scans every anchor, at a real cost.

items.description: Bare label value or complete label ref returned by KMP.

selectors.description: All predicates must hold on the whole entry's key-to-values labels. mode/include/exclude/scope_ids instead keep an entry when any coordinate passes: exclude task is not task notexists. Hard filters hide evidence; read kmp_wake.labels first.

op.description: in: any value under key is listed. notin: none is; an absent key passes. exists/notexists: key present/absent, with values empty.

items.description: Bare value from kmp_wake.labels; namespaced scope ids normalize to bare values.

request.description: Response paths supplied by the caller, not conclusions from stored memory.

selection.description: Response paths based on the temporal selection declared in proof; requested dimensions also apply. Proof may explicitly identify outside matches or omitted evidence.

path.description: The store this session opened. A wake that finds nothing speaks for this store only.

rule.description: The selection rule that chose it: env, project, worktree, saved, user or user fallback.

summary.description: Four-line L0 resume summary: objective, status, blocker, and next action.

causal_spine.description: Highest-salience explanatory relations, each with claim and because, plus evidence_refs to proof.evidence ids or inline evidence when no stored source holds it.

current_state.description: State lines from about context, not a historical-state answer; see scope.context.

guardrails.description: Stored constraints the continuation should preserve.

next_actions.description: Next-action statements reflected by the L0 summary; empty means no concrete next action was identified.

objective.description: The continuation intent supplied by the caller.

open_loops.description: Live blocker statements reflected by the L0 summary; empty means no blocker was identified.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Retrieve cited stored text and evidence, or UNKNOWN; never generate an answer. Read proof.evidence[].text and judge whether it answers. A dated semantic question uses as_of or a half-open UTC interval and axis; proof records the selection and nearest_outside on a bounded UNKNOWN. If the first English question finds UNKNOWN or irrelevant evidence, re-ask at most once in the user's own words. Changing optional arguments is another selection, not pagination; continue only through projection.page.next_cursor with bound arguments unchanged. After those selections, reclassify the original goal: history/current state uses temporal navigation; genuinely semantic UNKNOWN is terminal. Do not inspect the root, widen scope or traverse the graph to bypass it. proof.confidence measures lexical overlap, not answer correctness or relation-writer certainty; reached_by items are supporting proof, not direct answers. See proof fields for language-bridge and summary provenance. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic ask.
tools.name: kmp_ask

answer.description: UNKNOWN when the selected policy found no answerable evidence; otherwise names the retrieved citations without claiming they prove the answer.

answer_status.description: Present unless the store opted out of the anchored ask gate (ask-gate.json mode off). answered: the page holds the cited core and offers no continuation; projection.more_on_request counts the rest, paged with budget.detail full. partial: an enumerative question whose citations state part of it; proof.missing names the rest, confidence at most medium.

asked_as.description: The user's own words, echoed byte for byte when the request carried them. Absent otherwise.

because.description: At most five retained citation refs. Empty beside UNKNOWN; canonical text lives in proof.evidence.

Medium at most when the question reached the evidence through the lexical-bridge table rather than in its own words; not capped when the writer's English summary_en carried it.

summary.description: States whether nothing was retrieved, retrieved evidence did not bear on the question, or evidence was retained.

unknown_reason.description: Why the gate answered unknown; present with answer_status unknown. anchor_absent_in_selection means no memory read here names the identifier, not that none is stored; proof.missing names it.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Read what the memories of several abouts have to do with each other, off what they share and without declaring anything. Coordinate comparisons read the dimension scopes two abouts both use and where on one clock each memory stands inside them; they do not declare links. A writer may separately declare only `same_event_as` or `same_entity_as` across abouts, with a returned proposal and explicit proof, without merging their ownership. Returns the facts of the selected abouts within the interval with the lifecycle state they had at its end, the declared relations in the selection, including permitted cross-about equivalences, coordinate relations between facts of different abouts inside a scope they share (before, after, during, concurrent, same sequence, same rank, or merely the shared scope), tensions: facts that still stand and that a declared `contradicts` joins, and proposed links: pairs of facts of different abouts that share a key — an identifier rare across the span, an English summary that matches, a proper name — each with the signals that read it and a weight, never stored; a writer may use a returned proposal to declare an equivalence only when source evidence justifies identity. Nothing is ranked by a question and nothing is generated; every relation and every proposal says why in one sentence a reader can check. Pages by position over facts, declared, coordinate, tensions and proposed in that order. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic relate.
tools.name: kmp_relate

coordinate.description: Relations between facts of different abouts read off their coordinates inside a label they share — the same `dimension` kind and the same bare `scope_id`: `from`, `to`, `kind` (`shares_scope`, `before`, `after`, `during`, `concurrent`, `same_sequence`, `same_rank`), `dimension`, `scope_id`, the `axis` read, and `why` in one checkable sentence. The same scope under two kinds is two labels and relates nothing. Declared by nobody.

declared.description: Stored relations cut to the selection, with class, why, evidence and confidence. Includes writer-declared same_event_as and same_entity_as across abouts; other relations remain within their owning about.

facts.description: The entries of the selected abouts within the selection: `ref`, `about`, `kind`, `text` verbatim, `coordinates`, and `state` — `current`, `superseded` (with `superseded_by`) or `expired` (with `valid_until`) — as the lifecycle stood at the end of the interval.

next_actions.description: tool/arguments calls that continue this exact selection or raise an insufficient byte allowance; a continuation is a {continuation} handle to the complete call. Empty at the end. Execute unchanged, without reconstructing filters or cursors.

has_more.description: More items remain; this page is incomplete.

next_cursor.description: Opaque relate cursor; repeat it as page.cursor with selection arguments unchanged. budget.max_bytes and page.entries may vary; changed selected content or arguments return a conflict with a complete restart action.

offset.description: Number of selected items already read before this page.

required_bytes.description: When no whole item fits, retry page.next_cursor with budget.max_bytes at least this allowance to make progress. Absent otherwise.

total.description: Total facts, declared, coordinate, tensions and proposed, by position in that order in the selection.

abouts_empty_in_selection.description: Searched abouts with no entry in the selected interval or effective at the selected instant; empty for an unbounded read.

abouts_selected.description: Abouts read under dimensions.scope, current one first. Refs retain ownership; this list distinguishes searched from unsearched abouts.

as_of.description: Selected instant, including the time resolved from a ref cursor; null if unrequested.

axis.description: Selected occurred/observed/ingested/validity clock, or default precedence; null at the memory's own frontier.

confidence.description: Unspecified: a relate reading ranks nothing by a question. `interval`, `axis`, `abouts_selected`, `abouts_empty_in_selection`, `superseded`, `expired` and, when nothing fell within the selection, `nearest_outside` are what it declares.

conflicts.description: Explicit contradictions whose entries are both still live; distinct from supersession.

evidence.description: Verbatim stored text; metadata.proof_role distinguishes claim from evidence. Retrieval metadata never changes that text. reached_by items are indirect proof, never answers or citations in because; reached_from, reached_via and reached_hops identify their route. On citations, bridged_terms names cross-language word pairs; restated_from and restated_via identify a writer-declared restatement; matched_via: summary and summary_terms identify words matched through the writer's English summary_en, not the canonical text.

expired.description: Entries past exclusive valid_until at the temporal cursor, recall as_of/interval end, or otherwise the memory's latest instant. Expiry needs no replacement.

frontier_size.description: Reachable items not returned; a signal to expand.

matched_relations.description: Typed relations contributing to ordering. Their prose may improve a match, never promote unrelated evidence into an answer.

missing.description: What was sought but not found: no retrieval or no evidence bearing on the question. Non-empty with UNKNOWN.

nearest_outside.description: On interval UNKNOWN, nearest match outside it: ref, time and axis. Distinguishes not then from not known; otherwise null.

superseded.description: Replaced entries with superseded_by and why. Historical state, distinct from contradiction; not current advice. An ask's core keeps those touching a cited memory; the rest page as section proof.superseded.

proposed.description: Pairs of facts of different abouts the kernel proposes are about the same thing, at most three per fact, strongest first: `from`, `to`, `proposed_by` (`identifier`, `summary`, `entity`, strongest first), the `shared` identifiers with the `idf` of the rarest across the span, the `shared_terms` and `bridged` concept pairs of matching summaries, the `entities` both name, the label both stand in as `dimension` and `scope_id`, the `weight` the signals sum to, and `why`. Reproducible bit for bit and never stored. These signals propose a comparison, not proven identity. A writer copies from, to and proposed_by into read_context.relate_proposals and supplies source-backed why and evidence before declaring an equivalence.

summary.description: How many facts of how many abouts were related on which clock, and how many relations of each kind; or that nothing fell within the selection, naming the nearest fact outside it.

tensions.description: Facts that both still stand and that a declared `contradicts` joins: `ref`, `other`, the label they share when they share one as `dimension` and `scope_id`, and the `why` and `evidence` of the declaration. Shown, never resolved.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Navigate memory history on one clock. move: rewind reads newest first, strictly before `from` or within `interval`; forward reads oldest first, strictly after `from` or within `interval`; goto returns the state at `at`; near returns the neighbourhood around `around`. Cursors take time, sequence or ref. Execute next_actions unchanged: they finish this packet's response pages first, then continue history with the same clock, dimensions and interval. page.has_more counts packet expansion; selection.has_more reports history outside it. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic time.
tools.name: kmp_time

dimensions.description: Per-dimension returned counts and presence flags.

included.description: Dimension scope ids included in the result.

missing.description: Requested dimension scope ids not present in the result.

requested.description: Dimension selection requested by the caller.

entries.description: Temporal entries in traversal order. ref/kind always remain; fields selects text, coordinates and metadata. Each reduced entry has an executable detail_action for a fresh full selected-packet read with the original verb, cutoff, interval, scope, window and limits. Replay a shared action once, not once per entry.

next_actions.description: Execute these calls unchanged. While page.has_more, reconstruct this packet first; once complete, these calls navigate remaining history (Near can offer both directions).

arguments.description: Complete bound arguments, including the continuation cursor or a required budget adjustment.

has_more.description: More items remain; this page is incomplete.

minimum_progress_bytes.description: Present when the next complete item cannot fit. next_actions supplies a retry with this budget that admits at least one item.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for page.cursor; execute the complete next_actions call.

offset.description: Expansion items reconstructed before this page.

sections.description: Per-section returned_on_page and remaining; a zero counter and a section with none are omitted. Append each section across pages before concluding from proof.

total.description: Total entry and proof expansion items in the selection.

abouts_empty_in_selection.description: Searched abouts with no entry in the selected interval or effective at the selected instant; empty for an unbounded read.

abouts_selected.description: Abouts read under dimensions.scope, current one first. Refs retain ownership; this list distinguishes searched from unsearched abouts.

as_of.description: Selected instant, including the time resolved from a ref cursor; null if unrequested.

axis.description: Selected occurred/observed/ingested/validity clock, or default precedence; null at the memory's own frontier.

confidence.description: Temporal reads use medium when entries were returned and unknown when none were returned; this is not relation-writer certainty.

conflicts.description: Explicit contradictions whose entries are both still live; distinct from supersession.

entries.description: With include.dependencies, full stored dependency records with coordinates admitted by the proof boundary. These support the selected entries; they are not additional matches in the history window. fields does not shorten proof entries.

evidence.description: Verbatim stored text; metadata.proof_role distinguishes claim from evidence. Retrieval metadata never changes that text. reached_by items are indirect proof, never answers or citations in because; reached_from, reached_via and reached_hops identify their route. On citations, bridged_terms names cross-language word pairs; restated_from and restated_via identify a writer-declared restatement; matched_via: summary and summary_terms identify words matched through the writer's English summary_en, not the canonical text.

expired.description: Entries past exclusive valid_until at the temporal cursor, recall as_of/interval end, or otherwise the memory's latest instant. Expiry needs no replacement.

frontier_size.description: Reachable items not returned; a signal to expand.

groups.description: With include.dependencies, bounded writer-declared neighborhoods. Members resolve in entries or proof.entries after all pages. Source passages and typed links remain in proof.evidence/path. Anonymous counts describe only the selected scoped graph, never semantic sufficiency.

max_hops.description: Maximum expansion hops from this seed.

member_refs.description: Seed and available dependency entries in deterministic discovery order.

omitted_by_limit.description: Distinct eligible frontier members not expanded because of hop or member limits.

unavailable_in_selection.description: Distinct endpoints without an eligible body under this read; identities are not disclosed.

matched_relations.description: Typed relations contributing to ordering. Their prose may improve a match, never promote unrelated evidence into an answer.

missing.description: What was sought but not found: no retrieval or no evidence bearing on the question. Non-empty with UNKNOWN.

nearest_outside.description: On interval UNKNOWN, nearest match outside it: ref, time and axis. Distinguishes not then from not known; otherwise null.

superseded.description: Replaced entries with superseded_by and why. Historical state, distinct from contradiction; not current advice. An ask's core keeps those touching a cited memory; the rest page as section proof.superseded.

quality.description: Response-shape metrics; null when the backend supplied none.

causal_density.description: Share of returned relations that explain rather than merely connect; reflects the stored writing.

detail_coverage.description: Share of returned nodes that carry stored detail.

raw_refs.description: Typed raw audit refs for selected entries when include.raw_refs=true.

entries.description: Entries selected for this packet before response pagination.

included.description: Fields returned on each entry; ref and kind always remain.

omitted.description: Entry fields available through each returned detail_action; omitted fields are not empty values.

has_more.description: More matching history remains outside this packet. Complete its response pages before following the returned navigation actions.

matching_entries.description: Matching temporal entries reported by the kernel before its entry/window limit.

requested_refs.description: Present with refs: the explicit entry focus. Dependency records may have other refs within the same scope and time.

scope.description: selected_packet: top-level summary, coverage and quality refer to this bounded selection, not the current response page or all memory.

unmatched_ref_count.description: Requested refs not matching this history selection; may be absent, out of scope/filter/clock/direction. Does not prove nonexistence. Independent of response-page completion.

summary.description: Concise description of the temporal selection.

temporal.description: Direction, clock axis and entry interval. requested/resolved are null for a direct interval without an initial cursor.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Choose one mode: to connects known destination refs; search.seek discovers compatible evidence paths from a seed without destinations. Never combine their search options. A to array, search or temporal selection enables a bounded shared search through same-about entries. One shortest discovered route per destination by default; search can retain alternatives and follow each relation type in its chosen direction; paths do not establish answer completeness. A single to without search or temporal selection traces equivalence-aware over every stored relation with a bounded bidirectional search; a work cutoff returns no path, the stop in search and an optional search.widen. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic audit.
tools.name: kmp_trace

candidates.description: Seek paths with stable index, role, anchor, witness, context_hops, nodes and directed trace edge_indexes. Anchor is the main relation traversal start; witness is its other endpoint. Bindings give label/reference domains, roles and explicit endpoints when anchor equality is used; missing names exact witness refs and keys. Paths outside groups cannot jointly satisfy the request. clock_unknown keeps historical presence unproven. Join all pages.

expansion_refusal.description: Present only when a named expansion was refused before any body was read. code is read_selection_changed, with the expected and actual manifest, or unknown_expansion_refs, with the refs named outside this selection. Either way the response has no object, no support and no text: a partly valid batch delivers nothing. Repeat the original read without proof_refs or expect_selection to obtain the current manifest.

gaps.description: Per-ref missing_ref, missing_body, incomplete_entry and clock_unknown reasons. A work cutoff is incomplete retrieval, not evidence of absence.

groups.description: Compatible joint alternatives with stable index, candidate_indexes and intersected bindings. Missing values remain unknown even when another role has a known domain; clock_unknown requires review. All indexes address the complete tables, not a page. Multiple proofs of the same bindings need not mean ambiguity.

next_actions.description: tool/arguments calls that continue this exact selection or raise an insufficient byte allowance; a continuation is a {continuation} handle to the complete call. Empty at the end. Execute unchanged, without reconstructing filters or cursors.

objects.description: Shared selected entries and typed sources: exact available body, ref, kind, canonical snapshot status (not historical lifecycle), source metadata, source time, support clocks, admitted coordinates, hash/revision and has_body. Missing bodies are marked; summary text with has_body=false is not the full source.

has_more.description: More items remain; this page is incomplete.

next_cursor.description: Opaque trace cursor; repeat it as page.cursor with selection arguments unchanged. budget.max_bytes and page.entries may vary; changed selected content or arguments return a conflict with a complete restart action.

offset.description: Number of selected items already read before this page.

required_bytes.description: When no whole item fits, retry page.next_cursor with budget.max_bytes at least this allowance to make progress. Absent otherwise.

total.description: Total trace relations in the selection.

proof.description: Present with search.proof. expansion_plan names the next batch of bodies to ask for, decided over the complete selection before this response was paginated, so a page that holds none of the pending refs still carries it; expand_bodies and expand_oversized_body are that plan as complete calls. They continue a suffix of the manifest order and never claim a selection is complete: join responses by ref against one manifest, and read every page before concluding a selection is exhausted. Counts missing refs/bodies, incomplete entries and unknown attachment clocks. complete_groups/incomplete_groups index the declared target requirements or seek groups and describe fetched sources, not truth, lifecycle status or semantic sufficiency; a group whose body was deferred, not requested or shown as a card is not fetched proof. Join all pages and retain seek review_required/unknown. stop_reason and body_bytes report joint materialization work; body_bytes counts canonical UTF-8 bytes actually loaded, never a body this response withheld. With a body option active it also carries manifest_id, delivery counts and, for a compact read, the card summary.

condense_candidates.description: Compact proof orientation over the whole selection, identical on every page. Items rank by shared_by descending, body_bytes descending, then ref; at most 8 bodies of at least 1024 UTF-8 bytes. The floor is a heuristic, not a savings guarantee. Counts are disjoint: valid and after_cut take precedence over below_floor; objects without a stored body are outside these counts. Read the canonical body before authoring a card; copy source and expect into kmp_condense with this about, ref, compact language and scope node_body. This is not fetched proof or a required next action. A card written now cannot help a past cutoff.

shared_by.description: Returned routes, or seek groups with known clocks and all binding witnesses, whose selected proof uses this ref, once per route/group. Groups retained for review do not count; canonical body delivery is independent.

quality.description: Response-shape metrics; null when the backend supplied none.

causal_density.description: Share of returned relations that explain rather than merely connect; reflects the stored writing.

detail_coverage.description: Share of returned nodes that carry stored detail.

routes.description: Present in bounded mode. Each candidate has a target and zero-based edge_indexes into the complete trace table, in traversal hop order. Join every page first. Start at search.from and match each stored endpoint to reconstruct traversal direction. An empty index list is a zero-hop route to from. With search.select, only selected candidate paths and their complete relations are returned.

search.description: Present for bounded mode, and for a single to only when a work limit cut its bidirectional search (direction bidirectional, the destination unreached): widen is then the same bidirectional trace over every relation with the largest allowance, an optional full call, not a page continuation, and the cutoff is not absence. Stop reason distinguishes targets_reached, frontier_exhausted, node/edge/depth/state_budget and source_outside_selection. Optional routing reports dimensional checks/rejections, priority/FIFO pops and preferred_route_entries aligned with returned routes (including source). dimension_focus_pages_v2 alternates pages of at most four raw relations with child exploration, retaining exact positions and cached alternative rows. Routing also reports adjacency_pages, coordinate_pages and resumed_states (expansion turns of an already started path). It never drops a state by score; no shortest-path guarantee. Reading a page or its label coordinates can still exhaust N/E before a useful state expands. Optional material reports candidate count, selected original indexes, material nodes, covered/incomplete group indexes, benefit and selection work. Group indexes follow supplied groups; without groups they follow sorted target refs. expand_candidates is an optional full call starting a new selection without select, not a page continuation. Zero selected paths can mean no group fit, even with candidates available. Includes work counters, source from, direction (per_relation when follow is used), follow moves and paths_per_target. unreached_targets have no route; incomplete_targets have fewer than their quota. targets_reached means quotas obtained; the source needs only its zero-hop route. Frontier/leaf exhaustion is relative to selected direction, types and about; it proves no semantic answer. coordinate_rows are included in scanned_edges. A false temporal_selection_resolved means the ref cut could not be resolved within budget. clock_unknown_edges index undated selected links and do not prove those links existed at the cut.

seek.description: Seed evidence selection: status compatible, ambiguous, review_required, missing_obligation, incompatible_obligations or partial. declared_obligations_complete describes path/witness constraints, independently of proof source availability, and is always false for contextual discovery; it never means answer completeness or unique identity. Reports missing_roles, work/cut counters, role order and complete candidate/group counts. Optional review_context is a new scoped Goto read, separate from mandatory page continuations. Source materialization is optional through search.proof; semantic inference is never performed.

summary.description: Concise statement of the path selection.

supports.description: Eligible typed source-to-entry attachments with original arrows, why/evidence and clocks. Join through refs to objects and routes/candidates; a shared source is returned once.

trace.description: Typed relation table. In bounded mode, routes index this complete table after all pages are joined; empty at a work cutoff does not prove no path.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Inspect one stored memory object or accepted write receipt inside an explicit about boundary. Receipt object.text is immutable command-detail JSON, not current memory. Evidence, links and raw records page under the byte ceiling; continuations can reuse the first page's object. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic audit.
tools.name: kmp_inspect

evidence.description: Direct stored evidence for the object; text is canonical and supports names the refs it anchors.

incoming.description: Direct typed relations whose target is the inspected ref.

outgoing.description: Direct typed relations whose source is the inspected ref.

next_actions.description: Calls that continue the same inspection, including an increased byte allowance when no whole item fits. Execute unchanged, in order, and retain earlier pages; empty when complete.

arguments.description: {continuation}, a handle the server resolves to the complete call preserving about, ref, include and object reuse; or that complete call.

object.description: Stored object with ref, kind, canonical text, metadata, and optional source. With page.repeat_object=false, contains only ref; reuse the first page's object.

object_reused.description: Present and true only when this continuation omits the unchanged object body. Retain the first page's full object; the cursor validates it against the current selection.

guidance.description: Continuation, narrowing and budget guidance when this response is partial; null for a complete first page.

has_more.description: Whether expansion items remain after this page.

minimum_progress_bytes.description: Present only when this page cannot return an expansion item. The next action offers at least this allowance, preferring the complete inspection up to the usual 10,000-byte budget. required_bytes still measures the complete inspection.

next_cursor.description: Opaque inspect cursor. Repeat the same bound arguments with this value in page.cursor.

offset.description: Number of expansion items reconstructed by earlier pages.

required_bytes.description: Exact serialized bytes required by the complete inspection including its full object, even when this continuation reuses that object.

returned.description: Number of expansion items returned on this page.

sections.description: Per-section returned_on_page and remaining; a zero counter and a section with none are omitted. A section's total is its earlier pages plus both.

total.description: Total evidence, outgoing-link, incoming-link and raw expansion items in the selection.

quality.description: Response-shape metrics; null when the backend supplied none.

causal_density.description: Share of returned relations that explain rather than merely connect; reflects the stored writing.

detail_coverage.description: Share of returned nodes that carry stored detail.

raw.description: Typed raw audit records returned only when include.raw=true.

summary.description: Concise statement of which typed object was inspected.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Change the labels one memory stands in without rewriting its text: labels to add, labels to take off, and why. The kernel reads the memory's coordinates and the about's catalogue itself, so name pairs, never coordinates. A label added late inherits the memory's clocks — its time does not move — and its own instant lives on the edge it added, as `method: kmp_relabel` with your `why`; the event log keeps who did it when. Refused, naming what the memory stands in: a label it already stands in, one it does not, and taking its last label off. A new label that resembles one the catalogue holds is refused under strict and written with a warning otherwise, unless its key is in `options.labels_new`. Normal calls commit; `options.dry_run` validates against the store and writes nothing. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic write.
tools.name: kmp_relabel

accepted.description: True when the kernel committed the change; false on a dry run.

labels.description: The labels as pairs `{ key, value }`: `added` and `removed` by this call, `now` every label the memory stands in afterwards, `created` the added labels the about had never held — vocabulary growing, so make sure it was meant — and `resembling` the added labels that resemble one the about already holds, each with why.

created.description: Added labels the about had never held before.

now.description: Every label the memory stands in after the change, by key then value.

resembling.description: Added labels that resemble one the about holds: `key`, `value`, `existing_key`, `existing_value`, `kind` and `why`.

next_suggested_reads.description: The reads that show the change: `kmp_inspect` on the memory with `include.raw`.

summary.description: What changed and how many labels the memory stands in now.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Write your own compact card for one stored body, so later reads of the same paths can show the card instead of the whole body. Entries and the evidence sources of the same about can both be condensed, which matters because a source shared by several paths is usually the largest record on them. The card is your derived view, never canonical memory and never proof: it stands only for the body version you declare, and a later write makes it stale rather than wrong. Accepted revisions are preserved in event history and survive export/import and rebuild without changing the canonical body. Declare the revision and record digest the read gave you; a body that moved under you is refused with both versions named. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic condense.
tools.name: kmp_condense

authored_at.description: Kernel-stamped instant. A historical read at an earlier cut does not show this card.

card_revision.description: This card's own revision. Declare it in expect to replace this card.

source_body_bytes.description: Canonical UTF-8 bytes of the body it stands in for.

source_content_hash.description: Public token of that body version.

source_record_digest.description: Record digest this card is bound to.

source_revision.description: Body revision this card stands for.

status.description: Always valid for a freshly written card: it describes the body version it was just checked against.

text_bytes.description: Bytes of the stored card text.

summary.description: Which card revision was stored, for which entry, language and body revision.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Read where this store's memories stand with respect to their English search summaries, so the one writer that can produce a summary can see what to repair. Deterministic and repeatable: it reads the store's own event log, generates no text, changes nothing and never rejects a memory. Each entry returns a state — missing, refused, stands, not_required — with the lint's own faults when a summary is refused, and deterministic weakness signals when one stands and still retrieves little. Both feed kmp_write_memory search_summaries unchanged: render the text again and attach it. Scope defaults to one about; dimensions.scope abouts reads a named set and all_abouts sweeps every anchor, at a real cost. Page with page.cursor and the same bound arguments; totals describe the whole selection, not the page. It judges form, never meaning: a fluent, wrong summary passes, exactly as the lint does, unless the store opted into TypeSafe Jev, which reads each standing summary on the page against its memory and flags it `unfaithful`. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic condense.
tools.name: kmp_summaries_audit

abouts.description: The same counts per about, in the order the store met them.

about.description: The about these counts are for.

entries.description: Memories read.

missing.description: With no summary, whose text an English question cannot reach.

not_required.description: With no summary and no need of one.

owed.description: missing plus refused: the memories `kmp-mcp summaries pending` lists and the doctor counts.

refused.description: Carrying a summary the lint refuses.

stands.description: Carrying a summary the lint accepts.

weak.description: Of those that stand, how many carry at least one weakness signal. Never counted as owing a summary.

entries.description: One memory per item, in the order the store met them, filtered by states and cut by the page.

about.description: The about that owns this memory.

faults.description: Why the lint refuses this summary, in the lint's own words — the same sentences kmp_ingest and kmp_write_memory put in front of a writer. Present only in the refused state.

ref.description: The memory ref. Pass it back in kmp_write_memory search_summaries[].ref, byte for byte.

state.description: missing: no summary and an English question cannot reach the text. refused: a summary the lint will not accept, so it carries no retrieval. stands: the lint accepts it. not_required: no summary and none is needed, because the text is already in the kernel's search language.

summary_en.description: The stored English rendering, when there is one.

summary_en_by.description: Who wrote that rendering, when the store knows. This is what makes "regenerate everything an older writer produced" answerable.

text.description: The stored text, byte for byte, present only when this memory needs a rendering written — a debt, or a summary that stands weakly. Render this; never alter it to fit a summary.

weaknesses.description: Deterministic signals that this accepted summary still carries little retrieval. Warnings, never refusals: the memory is intact and the fix is a better rendering.

says.description: What to change, in one sentence.

signal.description: thin: it clears the lint's floor and little more, for a much longer text. repeated: other memories of this about carry it word for word. undiscriminating: every informative word of it already reaches most of this about's other memories. stale: the text was rewritten after the summary was last written. unfaithful: on a store opted into TypeSafe Jev, Jev does not read the summary as saying what the memory says.

jev.description: On a store opted into TypeSafe Jev: the model, requests and input tokens of the meaning check over this page's standing summaries.

next_actions.description: The complete call that continues this reading. Execute it and retain the earlier pages; empty when the reading is complete.

arguments.description: The complete call, with every bound argument preserved and page.cursor set.

has_more.description: More items remain; this page is incomplete.

next_cursor.description: Opaque audit cursor for page.cursor, or null. Repeat every bound argument unchanged; only page.entries and budget.max_bytes may vary. A changed selection rejects the cursor rather than paging a different reading.

offset.description: Memories already read by earlier pages of this continuation.

required_bytes.description: Present only when the stable response floor or its next whole memory exceeded the byte ceiling and was returned anyway. It is the exact serialized size of this complete structuredContent response; raise budget.max_bytes to it to avoid that overrun.

total.description: Total memories in the selection after the states filter in the selection.

abouts.description: The abouts the selection named. Empty for all_abouts, which names none.

selection.description: current_about, abouts or all_abouts — the scope this reading applied.

summary.description: What this reading covered and how much of it owes a summary.

totals.description: Counts over the whole selection, before any states filter and independent of paging. The doctor prints these, from this same reading.

entries.description: Memories read.

missing.description: With no summary, whose text an English question cannot reach.

not_required.description: With no summary and no need of one.

owed.description: missing plus refused: the memories `kmp-mcp summaries pending` lists and the doctor counts.

refused.description: Carrying a summary the lint refuses.

stands.description: Carrying a summary the lint accepts.

weak.description: Of those that stand, how many carry at least one weakness signal. Never counted as owing a summary.

warnings.description: Non-empty warnings qualify success; retain them.

tools.description: Review the relations of one or several abouts with the calling agent as author and TypeSafe Jev as a second reader. `mode: review` reads the selection the way kmp_relate does and writes nothing. It returns `missing`: pairs of current facts nothing declares yet — paired by the kernel from checkable signals (rare identifiers, summaries, names, shared labels), inside one about or across abouts, or picked by Jev for facts nothing else paired — each with the relation type Jev would choose, or `contradicts` when the two cannot both be true; and `suspect`: declared relations whose why and evidence Jev does not find supporting, or that Jev would type differently. Jev only chooses among offered options and judges text; it never writes a relation or a word of one, so every why and evidence you declare is yours, and a suggested type is a suggestion. Across abouts only same_event_as and same_entity_as are ever suggested. Jev is opt-in per store: `typesafe.json` beside the store and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in the environment; fact text of the selection is sent to TypeSafe. Without it the review returns kernel pairs untyped and audits nothing. The review is frozen under `review_token`; page it with that token and `page.cursor`. `mode: apply` takes items of a frozen review with your why and evidence; Jev reads your text once more, and which way round the relation runs, and withholds what it doubts until you correct or confirm it; the rest goes through kmp_write_memory's own plan, neighbourhood review and idempotency, and a needs_review answer resumes here. Only items whose `from` belongs to `about` are written by a call. `mode: paths` reads a whole selection — one about or several — keeps the facts Jev judges on the way from `from` to `to` (with `to`, only among at most 22 facts linked within four hops of either end), asks it for each one's direct consequence, and joins those steps to the declared relations into whole chains; proposed steps are frozen under `review_token` like missing relations. Embedded store only. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic curate.
tools.name: kmp_curate

accepted.description: True only when the canonical ingest was committed; false for a preview or pending context review.

evidence.description: Evidence nodes created by this write. Their ids are derived from the logical write identity and the triple, so an exact retry replays onto the same node and a later link to the same pair adds a new one instead of overwriting it.

relations.description: Links this relation-only write brought into existence: from, rel, to, class, confidence, the observation the link itself carries, and the evidence node created with it. Absent observed_at means the kernel stamped its ingestion instant, never an endpoint's clock.

unchanged_sources.description: The endpoint refs this relation-only write leaves untouched. Source text, evidence, coordinates, labels, metadata and ingestion history are not rewritten.

avoided.description: paths: declared relations the walk left out because Jev found their why and evidence do not hold (`from`, `to`, `rel`, `support`). Audit them with `mode: review`.

entries.description: Memories needing implicit observation, counted once across labels.

observed_at.description: ingested_at: omitted/null observation is resolved by the kernel. Previews describe a plan, never a committed timestamp.

provenance.description: Packet provenance also defaults to this write's ingestion time; search-summary updates preserve original fact clocks.

entries.description: Memories covered by this command.

distinct_values.description: Distinct instants carried by those memories.

entries.description: Memories with this clock, counted once across their memberships.

complete.description: All declared records and label memberships validated; accepted determines persistence.

label_memberships.description: Declared per-memory key/value pairs after shared-label union.

preserved_memberships.description: Existing memberships preserved by search_summaries. Omitted for relations, which do not enumerate or rewrite source coordinates; attachment.unchanged_sources names the untouched endpoints.

scope.description: submitted_packet: coverage of the declaration only.

source_coverage.description: not_assessed: KMP cannot detect facts omitted by the writer.

curate.description: apply: `doubted` items Jev asks you to reread (`item_id`, `support`, `direction` — how strongly Jev reads it the way you wrote it —, `reasons` among `support`, `type` and `direction`, `suggested_rel`, `jev`) — withheld until you correct them or send `confirm_doubted` —, `rejected` items this call cannot write with the reason, the `jev` usage of the pre-write check, and `warnings`.

diagnostics.description: Planner diagnostics that qualify the write.

dry_run.description: Whether this response is a validated preview that wrote nothing.

expand_context.description: Native reads only for stored_abouts to expand omitted stored surroundings. Complete their relevant pages.

feedback.description: Validation signals. Codes and paths come from validation, not message parsing. A warning can accompany acceptance; never invent missing proof.

arguments.description: Complete arguments to execute that read.

tool.description: Supported reading move, not proof that the proposed relation holds.

allowed_values.description: Valid vocabulary when the refused field has one; choose using the source, never automatically substitute a kind.

expected_type.description: JSON type required by an INVALID_TYPE refusal, such as array or object.

field.description: Argument path, for example memories[1].evidence; empty denotes the request as a whole.

reason.description: What must be corrected using actual sources.

received_type.description: Actual JSON type at the refused field; a JSON-encoded string remains string and is never coerced.

severity.description: error for a refusal; warning for accepted relations whose prior context needs review.

generated_refs.description: Stable refs generated for entries whose ref the caller omitted. Their identity suffix is deterministic for an exact logical-write retry and distinct across different writes.

ingest_preview.description: Canonical kmp_ingest arguments. Present only on dry-run.

jev.description: review: model, requests and input tokens spent; null when Jev was not used.

created.description: Of those, the labels the about did not hold before this write. Present only after a committed write; vocabulary grows here, so read it.

resembling.description: After a committed non-strict write: the labels written that resemble one the about already held, each with `key`, `value`, `existing_key`, `existing_value`, `kind` and `why`. Under strict such a write is refused instead, naming both labels, unless `options.labels_new` insists.

written.description: The labels this write carries, each `key` and `value`, in the order their coordinates were emitted.

local_refs.description: For a memories packet, local id to canonical memory ref. Preview refs are planned; accepted=true confirms persistence.

missing.description: review: pairs nothing declares: `item_id`, `from` and `to` as {ref, about, excerpt}, `suggested_rel` (Jev's choice among the types a writer may declare, or null without Jev), `proposed_by` (`kernel` or `jev`), the kernel `signals` and its `pairing_why` (null for Jev pairs), and `jev` {confidence, top three options}.

neighborhood.description: Bounded literal context: stored/proposed items, exact refs, clocks, reasons, omissions, token and complete stored_abouts ownership. Proximity does not prove a relation; expand partial stored context when needed.

next_actions.description: review: the call for the next page. apply after needs_review: the kmp_curate call that resumes this exact apply. Execute unchanged.

next_suggested_reads.description: Optional preview reading suggestions. Accepted writes need no routine verification; receipt.action retrieves audit detail on demand.

page.description: review: `entries`, `total` items in the review and `next_cursor`, null on the last page.

paths.description: paths: up to three chains, fewest proposed steps first: `hops` of {`from`, `to` as {ref, about, excerpt} in walking order, `rel`, `declared`, `reversed` when walked against its stored direction, `confidence`, and `item_id` for a proposed step, applicable with `mode: apply`}, plus `proposed` and `confidence`.

proposed_labels.description: labels: proposed memberships, strongest first: {`ref`, `key`, `value` among the values the about already uses, `confidence`, `excerpt`}. Apply the ones you confirm with kmp_relabel.

proposed_relations.description: Committed memories on a store with write-relations.json: relations Jev reads as missing from them, as `review_token`, `items` ({`item_id`, `from`, `to`, `rel`, `confidence`, `to_excerpt`}) and `jev`. Nothing is written: declare the ones you confirm with kmp_curate apply, in your own why and evidence.

read_after_write_ready.description: Whether a read now observes the accepted write.

arguments.description: Complete arguments. object.text holds JSON with receipt.canonical_memory, receipt.writer diagnostics and command revision/hash. It is a historical snapshot, not current graph state.

tool.description: kmp_inspect; execute only when accepted detail is needed.

ref.description: Immutable accepted-command audit ref. Absent for previews and simulated backends.

relation_quality.description: Preview per-relation validation. After commit, recover it with receipt.action.

relation_quality_metrics.description: Preview counts and prior-context coverage; stored in the receipt after commit.

relations.description: Compiled source -> relation -> target triples, in canonical ingest order. @id resolves through local_refs; other endpoints remain canonical refs. Review direction and scope against the source: acceptance does not prove semantic fidelity.

from.description: Source memory, the containing record in the request.

memories.description: Memories this packet wrote at a ref the caller supplied, each with the evidence this write put on it and the observation it now carries. A supplied ref replaces whatever that entry held; use relations to add a link without replacing a source.

review_token.description: review: the frozen review's token; pass it back to page or apply this review.

not_stored.description: Why no expansion could be judged or kept: nothing is stored unjudged.

refused.description: Each refused expansion as {ref, expansion, why}: the lint's fault or Jev's reading.

stored.description: Memory ref to the expansions kept, each read by Jev as belonging to it at the store's bar.

status.description: committed appended a command; replayed returned its earlier acceptance; validated is a preview; needs_review has applied nothing and returns context to review; rejected failed validation. unconfirmed cannot establish persistence: retain the logical key when resolving a transport failure.

summary.description: review: how many missing and suspect relations over how many current facts, and whether Jev was used. apply: what was written or why nothing was.

suspect.description: review: declared relations Jev doubts: `item_id`, `from`, `to`, the declared `rel`, `support` (Jev's probability that its why and evidence hold), `reasons` (`support`, `type`), `suggested_rel` and `jev`. Reported only; relations are never retracted here.

scope.description: current_store for a live embedded/gRPC preview; fixture for a simulated backend. A successful preview is not a reservation or a commit.

tell_the_user.description: One-time handoff text for the human; it is not another kernel instruction.

url.description: Loopback, read-only viewer URL carrying this session's capability.

warnings.description: Store notices qualifying this preview or accepted write; retain them.

tools.description: Open or rehydrate a ChronoLoom view over an about, so a human and this agent look at the same loom. Returns this session's capability link when the local viewer is mounted. Read-only with respect to memory: a view is a camera position, not a record. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic view.

applied.description: Whether this call is the one that moved the view. A replayed idempotency key answers false, and so does an intent none of whose named refs are in this store — `unhonored` then says so first and names every one of them.

clocks.description: The clocks the axis can read.

observability.description: How requested overlay series are queried and aligned on the view's temporal axis.

opened.description: Whether a view was opened or rehydrated.

reads.description: What this answer is, in the reader's terms.

state.description: The semantic view state: about, clock, focus, projection, selection, trace, paths (the kmp_curate paths answer the loom draws, with review_token and item_ids; null when none), search, and the provenance of the last change.

unhonored.description: What this call could not honor, in the caller's words: parts of the intent this build cannot render yet, and the refs it named that this store does not hold. Absence is always named here and never silently drawn, so read it even when the call succeeded.

tools.description: Move the view by declaring what it should show — focus, clock axis, semantic zoom, dimensions, relation classes, selection, trace, whole paths. Never pixels, coordinates or code. Atomic, idempotent, and under optimistic concurrency: if the person at the loom moved first, this conflicts and you rebase. Absence degrades rather than failing: a ref this store does not hold is dropped from the part that named it and listed in `unhonored`, and if none of the refs an intent names exist the view does not move at all and `applied` is false. Read `unhonored` — what is missing is always named there, never silently drawn. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic view.

tools.description: Open the brief capability map and persistent agent context. Start once with a unique registration_key; preserve the returned agent_id and context_id. Resume or expand a topic using context_id. After compaction use agent_id plus a new context_key, retaining the same agent. fold hides a topic without erasing its delivery record. This records served guidance, not understanding or authorization. Missing installed assets return explicit guide-sync repair instructions; preserve the selected store when applying them. Arguments explained: kmp_guide topic guide.

id.description: Stable opaque identity; preserve across contexts.

name.description: Random persistent display name; not an authorization credential.

card.description: One requested canonical worked card; null for the map or a fold.

parameters.description: Argument guide for each tool this topic teaches, one `path: description` line per documented argument. tools/list advertises types and constraints only.

relation_vocabulary.description: Topic write only: every writer relation as `name (quality; classes; when to use)`.

context_id.description: Exact token to resume this agent context.

durable.description: Whether agent metadata survives a server restart.

expanded.description: Topics opened in this context and revision, excluding folded ones.

guide_changed.description: This context previously used another guide revision; rediscover required topics.

guide_revision.description: Content revision used for this scheme and its delivery records.

next_actions.description: Complete optional calls for the extended verb.

scheme.description: Available topics; expanded lists the currently opened ones.

served.description: Topic cards and exact guide/example refs delivered in this context and revision; not learned or retained.

used.description: Observed work calls in this context and revision, never a learning score.
